blocks.text: 1. The Output Gate

blocks.alt: The cell state goes through tanh and the output gate to produce the hidden state

blocks.text: The Input Gate, the previous topic, decided what new information to add to the cell state. The Output Gate decides what to reveal from the cell state as the hidden state, explored in full depth throughout this topic.
It is LSTM's third and final gate, completing the full trio already previewed in LSTM Architecture, closing out coverage of every individual gate covered throughout this module.
2. Recapping The Preview

This connects back to the quick preview of all three gates, already covered in LSTM Architecture. The output gate was genuinely introduced there as the third and final gate, briefly described in that earlier topic.
This topic genuinely completes the full, dedicated treatment already given to the other two gates, closing out this module's three-part exploration of LSTM's own internal gating mechanism.
3. Cell State Versus Hidden State

blocks.alt: Cell state is long-term memory while hidden state is the exposed output

blocks.text: This connects back to the cell state idea, already covered in LSTM Architecture. A genuinely important distinction: the cell state is genuinely internal memory; the hidden state is what genuinely gets exposed.
The output gate genuinely controls exactly this exposure, the genuinely central role this gate plays throughout the rest of this topic.

blocks.text: 4. The Core Operation

The output gate's genuinely core operation connects back to the Sigmoid gating mechanism, already covered in LSTM Architecture. Compute a Sigmoid value from the current input and previous hidden state, exactly like the other two gates.
This directly reuses the exact same gating pattern already covered for both the forget gate and input gate, keeping LSTM's own overall design genuinely consistent across all three gates.
5. Applying Tanh To The Cell State

blocks.alt: Tanh squashes the cell state to the range -1 to 1

blocks.text: This connects back to Tanh, already covered in the Activation Functions module. First, apply Tanh to the genuinely updated cell state, already covered as the result of the forget and input gates.
This squashes it back into a genuinely bounded range, exactly the same range already covered for Tanh, keeping the exposed values genuinely well behaved before they become the new hidden state.
6. Combining For The Final Hidden State

blocks.alt: The output gate value multiplies the squashed cell state to produce the final hidden state

blocks.text: This connects back to combining both parts, already covered in The Input Gate. Multiply the output gate's own Sigmoid value by that Tanh-squashed cell state, element by element.
This produces the genuinely final hidden state that gets passed to the next time step and any output layer, mirroring the exact same multiply-to-combine pattern already covered for the input gate.

blocks.title: info
blocks.content: This same multiply-then-combine pattern, already covered in this topic, appears in all three gates: forget, input, and now output, a genuinely consistent, elegant design choice running throughout the entire LSTM architecture.

blocks.text: 7. Where The Output Goes

This connects back to output at every step, already covered in Vanilla RNN. This new hidden state genuinely feeds both the next time step's own computation and, when needed, a genuinely final prediction.
This is exactly the flexible output behavior already covered as Vanilla RNN's own design, now enriched by LSTM's own careful, gated memory management covered throughout this module.
8. Selective Exposure

blocks.alt: The full cell state is filtered by the output gate to give partial exposure

blocks.text: A genuinely important interpretive idea connects back to the compression limit, already covered in Hidden State. The output gate genuinely lets the network reveal only genuinely relevant parts of its own internal cell state.

This is a genuinely elegant solution to the fixed-size capacity limit already covered there, since the hidden state does not need to carry everything the cell state holds, only what is genuinely relevant right now.
9. Recapping All Three Gates Together

blocks.alt: The forget, input, and output gates chain together

blocks.text: This connects back to the forget gate and input gate, both already covered in their own topics. Forget decides what to discard, input decides what to add, output decides what to reveal.
Together, these three genuinely complete the LSTM cell already introduced in LSTM Architecture, forming the genuinely full, coordinated memory management system covered throughout this module.

blocks.text: 10. Recognizing Why The Output Gate Is Genuinely Essential

blocks.alt: Needing controlled exposure of memory points toward the output gate

blocks.text: This connects back to the cell state being genuinely internal memory, already covered in this topic. Without the output gate, already covered, that genuinely raw internal memory could never be genuinely usefully exposed.

Wanting genuinely selective, task-relevant information passed forward rather than everything at once is another genuine case where the output gate, already covered, directly provides exactly that selectivity.
11. Worked Example

The example below directly demonstrates the output gate's own full computation, applying Tanh to the cell state and combining it with the Sigmoid output, illustrating the concepts already covered throughout this topic.

code.content:
import numpy as np

def sigmoid(x):
    return 1 / (1 + np.exp(-x))

updated_cell_state = np.array([3.5, -2.0, 1.2, 4.8])  # already covered as the result of the forget and input gates

# already covered as the core operation in this topic
output_gate_value = sigmoid(np.array([1.0, -1.5, 2.0, 0.5]))

# already covered as applying Tanh to the cell state in this topic
squashed_cell_state = np.tanh(updated_cell_state)

# already covered as combining for the final hidden state in this topic
new_hidden_state = output_gate_value * squashed_cell_state

print(f"Updated cell state: {updated_cell_state}")
print(f"Output gate value: {np.round(output_gate_value, 3)}")
print(f"Tanh-squashed cell state: {np.round(squashed_cell_state, 3)}")
print(f"\nFinal hidden state (already covered in this topic): {np.round(new_hidden_state, 3)}")

blocks.title: info
blocks.content: Running this example shows the raw cell state first squashed through Tanh, then selectively revealed through the output gate's own Sigmoid values, exactly the two-step process already covered as this topic's own core mechanism.

blocks.text: 12. LSTM & GRU: Progress Recap

items: The output gate decides what to reveal from the cell state as the hidden state.
The cell state is internal memory; the hidden state is what actually gets exposed.
It computes a Sigmoid value from the current input and previous hidden state, like the other gates.
The updated cell state first gets squashed through Tanh into a bounded range.
Multiplying the Sigmoid output by that squashed cell state produces the final hidden state.
This new hidden state feeds both the next time step and any needed final prediction.
It provides selective exposure, revealing only what is genuinely relevant right now.
Together, forget, input, and output gates complete the full LSTM cell.
